In 125,474 US adults who started liraglutide, semaglutide or tirzepatide in 2018-2023, one-year discontinuation without type 2 diabetes was 64.8%. This is the book's obesity rate, reused from the Elecoglipron, VK2735, Eloralintide and Cagrilintide seeds (lookup.py seed)
column12: Reused, kept identical across the obesity claimants. The case against: in trials, aleniglipron's stopping rates are far lower. Treatment-related discontinuation was 10.4% across the active arms of the 36-week ACCESS trial (Nature Medicine 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04476-6). Fewer than 5% stopped for adverse events in the 72-week open-label extension on a 2.5 mg starting dose (8-K 2026-09-08). Real-world stopping, however, is driven by cost and access as much as by tolerability. The rate is also a first-year rate among new starters, applied here to the whole treated stock, so it overstates attrition in later years

column12: JUDGEMENT. Structure has published no filing or launch date. The Enicepatide seed uses retatrutide's measured interval of three to five months from final primary completion to submission. On that interval Structure would submit around early 2029, and a standard 12-month new-molecule review would bring approval around early 2030. That makes 2030 the first revenue year, the year the book gives Enicepatide (mid-2028 completions) and the verified Duvakitug row (September 2028 completion). The case for 2031: this would be Structure's first NDA. Novo's own interval from REDEFINE 1's completion to the CagriSema filing was 13.6 months (verified Zenagamtide row), which would put submission in late 2029. Structure's cash also runs only 'through the end of 2028' and 'excludes additional costs related to pre-commercialization activities including commercial manufacturing' (10-Q 0001104659-26-092057). The case for earlier: Foundayo was approved on 2026-04-01 under a national priority voucher (PharmExec; book approvals table, NDA220934). I found no voucher held by Structure. The book is not consistent here. Elecoglipron and AZD6234 take 2029 from their 2028 completions

column12: JUDGEMENT: 0.444x the incumbent, the rung the book gives VK2735. Its seed reasons: 'the molecule is competitive, the company has no salesforce and no formulary relationships'. Structure is in the same position. It has 'no internal sales, marketing or distribution capabilities, nor have we as a company commercialized a product' (10-Q 0001104659-26-092057). The analogy is direct. VK2735 is a small company's version of a form the incumbent already sells, a weekly injection against Zepbound. Aleniglipron is a small company's version of the oral small molecule Lilly already sells. Foundayo was approved on 2026-04-01 (book approvals table, NDA220934) and booked $98mm in its first quarter, Q2 2026 (book asset_revenue, 8-K exhibit 0000059478-26-000077). So aleniglipron gets none of the oral premium the book gives Elecoglipron (0.556x, 'an oral is a real advantage over a weekly injection'). That premium belongs to an oral against the injections. When aleniglipron launches around 2030, it would be at least the third oral GLP-1 for weight: after the Wegovy pill (approved 2025-12-22, Novo 6-K 0001171843-25-008080) and Foundayo, and alongside AstraZeneca's elecoglipron, seeded from 2029. Nor is it docked below VK2735. Its Phase 2 weight loss is at least the oral incumbent's: 11.3% placebo-adjusted at week 36 on 120 mg in ACCESS (PMID 42249138) and 16.3% at week 44 on 180 mg in ACCESS II (10-Q). Orforglipron 36 mg took 11.2% against 2.1% on placebo at week 72 in ATTAIN-1 (NEJM 2025, PMID 40960239, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2511774). That comparison crosses trials and sets Phase 2 against Phase 3, so the efficacy edge is not credited either. The case for lower, the next rung down: aleniglipron launches about four years behind the category leader's own oral, which comes with Lilly's payer contracts and a self-pay floor of $149 to $349 a month. It enters a pool the ten obesity seeds already in the book share. And Structure's cash covers the Phase 3 only through end-2028, excluding pre-commercial costs, so the launch depends on a raise or a partner. The case for higher, Elecoglipron's 0.556x: its efficacy sits near the top of the oral class. A small molecule scales in manufacture where peptide supply has been tight. A likely partner or acquirer would bring the salesforce this rung docks it for; Pfizer bought Metsera in November 2025, as the Berobenatide seed records. If a partner arrives, this rung should rise and economics_share should fall, both at once
